title: 12 Days: Reconquest of Spain and the Old Queen of Hawaii

sentences.en: Hello, welcome to The Rest is History, 12 Days of Christmas special.
sentences.zh: 你好，欢迎收看《历史的余韵》圣诞十二日特别节目。

sentences.en: And Dominic, today it's the 2nd of January.
Did anything important happen on the 2nd of January?
sentences.zh: 1月2日发生过什么重要的事情吗？

sentences.en: And if it did, is it perhaps Spanish-themed?
sentences.zh: 如果有的话，是不是和西班牙有关？
是的，确实和西班牙有关。

sentences.en: So it's a huge event in world history, Tom.
sentences.zh: 所以这是世界史上的一件大事，汤姆。

sentences.en: So you've been to Granada, I assume?
sentences.zh: 我想你应该去过格拉纳达吧？

sentences.en: It's a magnificent palace, for those people who don't know, on the rock overlooking the city, this great sort of ornament of Islamic Spain.
sentences.zh: 对于那些不知道的人，那是一座宏伟的宫殿，坐落在俯瞰城市的岩石上，是伊斯兰西班牙的一种伟大装饰。

sentences.en: And so what's called the Reconquista
sentences.zh: 那么所谓的“收复失地运动”

sentences.en: has been going on for centuries, effectively, the Christian reconquest of Spain.
sentences.zh: 实际上已经持续了几个世纪，即基督徒对西班牙的收复。

sentences.en: Now that in itself is quite a loaded term, and one I think that a lot of historians would be a little bit suspicious of now, don't you?
sentences.zh: 这个词本身就带有很强的倾向性，我想现在很多历史学家对此都会持怀疑态度，你不觉得吗？

sentences.en: Because, I mean, they would argue that it's not a kind of reconquest
sentences.zh: 因为他们会争辩说，这并不是一种“收复”，

sentences.en: so much as the creation of something that hadn't previously existed.
sentences.zh: 而更像是创造了一些以前不存在的东西。

sentences.en: I think it is a reconquest as well.
sentences.zh: 我认为这确实也是一种收复。

sentences.en: Do you think it's a reconquest?
It's a reconquest by Christian rulers of lands that had previously been Christian.
sentences.zh: 这是基督徒统治者对曾经属于基督教土地的收复。

sentences.en: Don't really have a problem with calling it out.
sentences.zh: 我并不觉得称其为收复有什么问题。

sentences.en: But that seems to, you see, what I don't like about that is that that seems to imply that the Islamic sort of societies that have been there were intruders, newcomers,
sentences.zh: 但你看，我不喜欢这一点，因为它似乎暗示了在那里存在的伊斯兰社会是入侵者、是后来者，

sentences.en: whereas they've been there for centuries.
sentences.zh: 而事实上他们已经在那里存在了几个世纪。

sentences.en: I mean, to use the example that I used in yesterday's podcast, they have been there for far longer than the United States has existed.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，用我在昨天播客中举的例子，他们在那里的时间比美国建国的时间还要长得多。

sentences.en: But I think that, I mean, the Reconquista is obviously a Spanish word coined by the Spanish Christians who themselves, and I think it adequately reflects
sentences.zh: 但我认为，“收复失地运动”显然是一个由西班牙基督徒自己创造的西班牙语词汇，我认为它充分反映了
他们是如何理解这个过程的。

sentences.en: It does, but you don't think it's loaded?
sentences.zh: 确实如此，但你不觉得这个词带有偏见吗？

sentences.en: You don't think it's very loaded?
sentences.zh: 你不觉得它非常带有偏见吗？

sentences.en: Well, I think there's a kind of desire on the part of people to see pre-Reconquista Spain as some multicultural paradise.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为人们有一种愿望，想把收复失地运动前的西班牙看作某种多元文化的乐园。

sentences.en: And I think that that was really, really bred of the tensions in the first decade of the 21st century.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为这实际上是源于21世纪头十年的紧张局势。

sentences.en: There was a real desire to say, yeah, there was a time where Muslims and Christians and Jews all got on really well, and they all sat around eating oranges and-
sentences.zh: 当时有一种强烈的愿望，想要说，是的，曾经有一段时期，穆斯林、基督徒和犹太人相处得非常好，他们坐在一起吃着橙子，还有——

sentences.en: Talking about Aristotle, bubbling fountains, all this kind of stuff.
sentences.zh: 谈论亚里士多德，冒泡的喷泉，诸如此类的事情。

sentences.en: Yes, and so the word Reconquista seemed, well, problematic in that context.
sentences.zh: 是的，所以“收复失地运动”这个词在那种语境下显得有些问题。

sentences.en: But I think that's a fantasy.
sentences.zh: 但我认为那是一种幻想。
基督教统治也极其残酷。
这个过程本质上就是战争。

sentences.en: The idea that there, you know, of course there were,
sentences.zh: 那种认为，你知道，当然有，

sentences.en: there was Jews and Christians and Muslims did commune because they all lived cheek by jowl.
sentences.zh: 犹太人、基督徒和穆斯林确实有过交流，因为他们都比邻而居。

sentences.en: There was kind of scholarly communication.
sentences.zh: 确实存在某种学术交流。

sentences.en: But in Muslim lands, Christians and Jews were decisively subordinate.
sentences.zh: 但在穆斯林土地上，基督徒和犹太人处于绝对的从属地位。

sentences.en: And in Christian lands, Jews and Muslims were decisively subordinate.
sentences.zh: 而在基督教土地上，犹太人和穆斯林也处于绝对的从属地位。

sentences.en: And I think the attempt to imagine that this was some kind of paradise is wholly bogus.
sentences.zh: 我认为试图将其想象成某种乐园是完全虚假的。

sentences.en: Well, we can get into this.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我们可以深入探讨一下。

sentences.en: The language of conquest, I think, is important because it reflects the brute realities of what we're going on.
sentences.zh: 我认为征服的语言很重要，因为它反映了当时发生的残酷现实。

sentences.en: We can get into this in more detail in a future podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 我们可以在未来的播客中更详细地讨论这个问题。

sentences.en: It's great to find a subject on which I can pretend to be more progressive.
sentences.zh: 能找到一个我可以假装自己更进步的主题真是太好了。

sentences.en: Let's get back to the anniversary.
sentences.zh: 让我们回到这个周年纪念日。

sentences.en: So the 2nd of January, 1492, the final war, really, in rolling up the Islamic kingdoms of southern Spain has been launched the previous April.
sentences.zh: 1492年1月2日，实际上，在去年四月发起的扫荡西班牙南部伊斯兰王国的最后战争。

sentences.en: And that's the Granada War, the attack on the last emirate, the last Islamic emirate.
sentences.zh: 那就是格拉纳达战争，对最后一个埃米尔国，最后一个伊斯兰埃米尔国的攻击。

sentences.en: And it's been launched, obviously, by Ferdinand and Isabella, the most Catholic monarchs, as they are known.
sentences.zh: 显然，这是由斐迪南和伊莎贝拉发起的，也就是众所周知的“天主教双王”。

sentences.en: So Ferdinand of Aragon and Isabella of Castile, who are going to unite to create Spain.
sentences.zh: 也就是阿拉贡的斐迪南和卡斯蒂利亚的伊莎贝拉，他们将联合起来创建西班牙。
总之，格拉纳达被孤立了。

sentences.en: Its allies have been defeated or basically lost their nerve.
sentences.zh: 它的盟友要么被击败，要么基本上失去了勇气。

sentences.en: So for what become the Spanish, it's actually a relatively easy job to kind of surround it and subdue it.
sentences.zh: 所以对于后来成为西班牙人的人来说，包围并征服它实际上是一项相对容易的工作。

sentences.en: The Granadans issue appeals to the Ottomans, to North Africa and so on.
sentences.zh: 格拉纳达人向奥斯曼帝国、北非等地发出求援。

sentences.en: But basically everybody ignores them because they know it's a kind of complete lost cause.
sentences.zh: 但基本上每个人都无视他们，因为他们知道这完全是死路一条。

sentences.en: Then there's a very strange kind of, it's almost like a kind of Brexit deal process.
sentences.zh: 然后发生了一种非常奇怪的事情，几乎就像某种英国脱欧式的协议过程。

sentences.en: the attackers agree a kind of pre-truce truce with the defenders.
sentences.zh: 进攻方与防守方达成了一种“停战前的停战协议”。

sentences.en: And they sort of say, well, we'll pause while we discuss the details of the truce.
sentences.zh: 他们大概是说，好吧，我们暂停一下，讨论停战的细节。

sentences.en: And then the final deal is done in time for the 2nd of January.
sentences.zh: 最终协议在1月2日之前达成。

sentences.en: And that's the day that even now in Granada, they celebrate it.
sentences.zh: 直到今天，格拉纳达还在庆祝这一天。

sentences.en: They have marches and processions and they have sort of this great fiesta because this is the death knell of Muslim Spain and the moment that a kind of new Spain is born.
sentences.zh: 他们有游行和队列，还有盛大的节日，因为这是穆斯林西班牙的丧钟，也是一个新西班牙诞生的时刻。

sentences.en: So the guy who is in charge of Granada, he's about in his early 30s, about 32.
sentences.zh: 当时负责格拉纳达的那个人，大约30出头，32岁左右。

sentences.en: And his name is, his actual name is Abu Abdallah Mohammed XII.
sentences.zh: 他的名字，他真正的名字是阿布·阿卜杜拉·穆罕默德十二世。
zh_words: 阿布·阿卜杜拉·穆罕默德

sentences.en: But he's known to Spanish chroniclers as Boabdil, sort of corruption of Abdallah.
sentences.zh: 但西班牙编年史家称他为博阿布迪尔，这是阿卜杜拉的一种讹传。

sentences.en: And Boabdil rides out with about 80 of his men on the 2nd of January to the camp on the banks of the river Genil, which is sort of facing the Alhambra,
sentences.zh: 1月2日，博阿布迪尔带着大约80名随从骑马前往赫尼尔河畔的营地，那里正对着阿尔罕布拉宫，
前往阿拉贡斐迪南的营地。

sentences.en: And then this sort of, this great sort of set piece.
sentences.zh: 然后是这种，这种盛大的场面。

sentences.en: By so many Spanish painters and so on, he hands over the keys to the city, to Ferdinand, basically in surrenders.
sentences.zh: 被许多西班牙画家描绘过，他把城市钥匙交给了斐迪南，基本上就是投降了。

sentences.en: And the great thing about this tableau, Tom, is that one of the people who is there and watching is Christopher Columbus,
sentences.zh: 这个场景最棒的地方在于，汤姆，当时在场观看的人之一就是克里斯托弗·哥伦布，

sentences.en: is a young Italian who has been pestering Ferdinand and Isabella to pay for his plans to go into India.
sentences.zh: 是一个年轻的意大利人，他一直缠着斐迪南和伊莎贝拉资助他前往印度的计划。

sentences.en: And of course, it's Christopher Columbus.
sentences.zh: 当然，那就是克里斯托弗·哥伦布。

sentences.en: And later on, we have a letter that Christopher Columbus writes to Ferdinand and Isabella when he's sucking up to them.
sentences.zh: 后来，我们有一封克里斯托弗·哥伦布写给斐迪南和伊莎贝拉的信，当时他在讨好他们。

sentences.en: And he says, I remember seeing the royal banners of your highnesses planted by force of arms on the towers of the Alhambra.
sentences.zh: 他说，我记得看到你们殿下的皇家旗帜在阿尔罕布拉宫的塔楼上通过武力插上。

sentences.en: So he's there watching this extraordinary landmark moment, which for a lot of people, I think you could say, is the end.
sentences.zh: 所以他当时就在那里，见证了这个非凡的里程碑时刻，对于很多人来说，我认为可以说这是终结。

sentences.en: It's one of those, when do the Middle Ages end?
sentences.zh: 这是那种“中世纪何时结束”的时刻之一。

sentences.en: I mean, this is one of those moments, the end of Islamic Spain, the moment that the balance, you could argue that the balance between the West
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是那些时刻之一，穆斯林西班牙的终结，你可以说这是西方与伊斯兰之间平衡的时刻，

sentences.en: and Islam, for want of a better expression,
sentences.zh: 如果用一个更好的表达方式的话，

sentences.en: Of course, you've got the high points of the Ottoman Empire to come.
sentences.zh: 当然，奥斯曼帝国的高光时刻还在后面。

sentences.en: And Spain is going to, of course, become the great superpower.
sentences.zh: 当然，西班牙将成为伟大的超级大国。

sentences.en: So there's one more moment, which is the moment.
sentences.zh: 所以还有一个时刻，就是那个时刻。
每个人都记得的那个时刻。

sentences.en: So if you've ever been to Granada, it's surrounded by mountains.
sentences.zh: 如果你去过格拉纳达，那里被群山环绕。

sentences.en: The Albu Haras, I think they're called.
sentences.zh: 我想它们叫阿尔普哈拉斯山脉。

sentences.en: We must want holiday up in the mountains.
sentences.zh: 我们一定想去山里度假。

sentences.en: Anyway, so he's winding up into the mountains, into Exar, because he's going to go to Morocco, to Fez, and spend the rest of his days in Fez.
sentences.zh: 总之，他正蜿蜒进入山区，进入埃克萨，因为他要去摩洛哥的非斯，并在非斯度过余生。

sentences.en: And the story goes, always told by Spanish kind of folklorists, that he stops at this kind of ridge, and he looks back over at the Alhambra, the great pink stone walls,
sentences.zh: 故事是这样说的，总是被西班牙的民俗学家讲述，他在这个山脊停了下来，回头望向阿尔罕布拉宫，那巨大的粉红色石墙，

sentences.en: in the dying sunlight, the sound of the fountains.
sentences.zh: 在垂死的阳光下，喷泉的声音。

sentences.en: The most beautiful buildings in the world.
This vision of Alhambra is created to be a paradise.
sentences.zh: 阿尔罕布拉宫的这种景象被创造出来作为天堂。

sentences.en: And it is a paradise, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 它确实是一个天堂，不是吗？

sentences.en: I mean, it is among the most beautiful buildings.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，它是最美丽的建筑之一。

sentences.en: And he looks back, and Boab Dylan, he weeps.
sentences.zh: 他回头看，博阿布迪尔，他哭了。

sentences.en: And his mother, his mum, says to him, I know.
sentences.zh: 他的母亲，他的妈妈对他说，我知道。

sentences.en: Now you weep like a woman over what you could not defend as a man.
sentences.zh: 现在你像个女人一样为你无法像个男人一样去保卫的东西而哭泣。

sentences.en: I mean, if your mum said that to you, you'd never recover.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，如果你的妈妈那样对你说，你永远都无法恢复。

sentences.en: I mean, that would scar you for life.
So that's called, I mean, his sigh, it's called The Moor's Last Sigh.
sentences.zh: 所以这被称为，我的意思是，他的叹息，被称为“摩尔人的最后叹息”。

sentences.en: So that's in the Salman Rushdie book.
sentences.zh: 那是在萨尔曼·拉什迪的书里。

sentences.en: And the pass, where he supposedly stops, it's called The Pass of the Moor's Sigh.
sentences.zh: 而他据称停下来的那个山口，被称为“摩尔人叹息之口”。

sentences.en: It's a very romantic story, but actually what then happens is pretty unromantic.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常浪漫的故事，但实际上接下来发生的事情一点也不浪漫。

sentences.en: So you get the sort of, the forcible conversion of a lot of the Moors, the Mooriscos.
sentences.zh: 所以你得到了那种，对许多摩尔人，即摩里斯科人的强制改宗。

sentences.en: Well, because actually the treaty is, it's pretty generous.
sentences.zh: 嗯，因为实际上条约是非常慷慨的。

sentences.en: And even Christians who've converted to Islam don't have to convert back.
sentences.zh: 甚至那些改信伊斯兰教的基督徒也不必改回来。

sentences.en: But the Spanish soon renege on that.
sentences.zh: 但西班牙人很快就违背了这一点。

sentences.en: And there starts to be this series of kind of forced conversions.
sentences.zh: 于是开始了一系列强制改宗。

sentences.en: So Mooriscos comes to the Mooriscos, exactly.
sentences.zh: 所以摩里斯科人，正是摩里斯科人。

sentences.en: Confiscation of property and so on.
A whole, I mean, one of the biggest, I mean, it goes on for ages.
sentences.zh: 整个，我的意思是，这是最大的之一，我的意思是，它持续了很久。

sentences.en: So one of the biggest waves of expulsions comes to the beginning of the 17th century.
sentences.zh: 所以最大的驱逐浪潮之一发生在17世纪初。

sentences.en: I mean, you're talking about a massive movement of people, refugee kind of crisis.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你在谈论大规模的人口流动，难民危机。

sentences.en: So tens of thousands of people going to North Africa.
sentences.zh: 所以成千上万的人前往北非。

sentences.en: So there are three kind of seismic events that happen in this year.
sentences.zh: 所以这一年发生了三件地震级的事件。

sentences.en: Columbus's voyage across the Atlantic and the expulsion of the Jews.
sentences.zh: 哥伦布横渡大西洋的航行，以及对犹太人的驱逐。

sentences.en: So actually the fall of Granada creates this momentum for a unified Christian Spain in which the Muslims and the Jews do not belong.
sentences.zh: 所以实际上格拉纳达的陷落为统一的基督教西班牙创造了动力，而穆斯林和犹太人并不属于其中。

sentences.en: And so you get the expulsion of the Jews who of course, you know, tens of thousands of people who end up going to Italy, to Greece, to North Africa.
sentences.zh: 于是你得到了对犹太人的驱逐，当然，你知道，成千上万的人最终去了意大利、希腊、北非。

sentences.en: And that's the origin of the kind of Sephardic Jewish branch.
sentences.zh: 那就是塞法迪犹太分支的起源。
这是一场大规模的流亡。

sentences.en: Into places like, you know, I don't know,
sentences.zh: 去往那些地方，你知道，我不知道，

sentences.en: And the Ottomans, of course, you know,
can't believe that the Spaniards are being so stupid.
sentences.zh: 无法相信西班牙人竟然如此愚蠢。

sentences.en: Expelling all these, you know, incredibly able and wealthy people.
sentences.zh: 竟然驱逐了所有这些，你知道，极其能干且富有的人。

sentences.en: I mean, to us, it seems, I mean, it's kind of the ultimate crime, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 我是说，对我们而言，这似乎，我是说，这简直是终极罪行，不是吗？

sentences.en: It seems a crime against a multicultural,
sentences.zh: 这似乎是对一个多元文化、

sentences.en: But it exists in the context of apocalyptic yearning, I think.
sentences.zh: 但我认为，这存在于一种末世渴望的背景之下。

sentences.en: I think Ferdinand seriously sees himself as a figure who may be destined to bring in the, you know, the second coming.
sentences.zh: 我认为费迪南德确实把自己视为一个注定要带来，你知道，第二次降临的人物。

sentences.en: He's very, very focused on the recapture of Jerusalem.
sentences.zh: 他非常、非常专注于收复耶路撒冷。

sentences.en: And Columbus, likewise, is very, very motivated by this kind of idea that, you know, the end of the world is drawing near.
sentences.zh: 同样，哥伦布也深受这种想法的驱动，你知道，世界末日即将来临。

sentences.en: And people's motives exist in the context that to us seems very, very hard to get a grasp on, I think.
sentences.zh: 我认为，人们的动机存在于一种我们觉得非常、非常难以理解的背景之中。

sentences.en: I mean, I read a book a year ago by a guy called Fernando Cervantes.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我一年前读过一个叫费尔南多·塞万提斯的人写的书。

sentences.en: I don't think he's related to the Cervantes.
sentences.zh: 我不认为他和那个塞万提斯有亲戚关系。

sentences.en: He's a Mexican historian and it's a book called Conquistadores.
sentences.zh: 他是一位墨西哥历史学家，那本书叫《征服者》。

sentences.en: What happens in the same year.
So basically the arrival of the Spanish in the new world.
sentences.zh: 基本上就是西班牙人抵达新世界。

sentences.en: And a lot of the, you know,
obviously a lot of the people who arrive in the new world have been in these campaigns.
sentences.zh: 显然很多抵达新世界的人都参加过这些战役。

sentences.en: So they have been fighting against the Moors and they are absolutely, one of the things that Cervantes really brings out in this book is he says, you know,
